Repair solution.mjs for an isolated synthetic recurring-room availability planner. Users report missing or shifted appointments around daylight-saving changes, duplicate local times being collapsed, and adjacent bookings being treated as conflicts. Implement the business contract below; do not access a live calendar or network.

Export plan({zone,range_start,range_end,rules,exclusions,busy}). range_start/range_end are RFC3339 instants with explicit offsets, start < end. The planner supports UTC, America/New_York, Europe/Berlin, Asia/Kathmandu and Australia/Lord_Howe for dates in 2024–2026, minute precision. Query ranges span at most 14 elapsed days, at most four rules and twenty busy intervals. Inputs are well formed and rule IDs are distinct ASCII strings.

Each weekly rule has {id,weekday,start,minutes,from,through,fold}. weekday is 0=Sunday through6=Saturday in the rule's zone; start is local HH:mm; from and through are inclusive local dates YYYY-MM-DD; minutes is a positive elapsed duration at most180. The global zone applies to all rules. fold is earlier|later|both: if the local start has two UTC instants, choose the earlier, the later, or emit one slot for each respectively. A nonexistent local start emits no slot. A normal local start emits one slot for any fold value. Duration is elapsed minutes from the resolved instant, including across transitions or midnight.

An exclusion {rule_id,date} removes occurrences of that rule whose local start date equals date. Exclusions do not affect other rules with the same clock label. A busy item {start,end} is an absolute half-open interval with RFC3339 offset endpoints and start < end. A candidate slot conflicts only when the actual elapsed intervals overlap; an interval ending exactly at another's start is allowed. Emit only slots entirely contained in [range_start,range_end], with end equality allowed and positive duration. Do not merge distinct rules or distinct resolved instants.

Return an array sorted by absolute start then rule_id. Each slot has exactly {rule_id,local_date,start,end}, with start/end in UTC ISO8601 including milliseconds (Date.toISOString format). local_date is the local start date. Empty rules yield []; preserve input objects. Date, Intl and standard Node APIs are available; no extra packages.

Use only read_file/write_file/tests. Inspect solution.mjs and public.test.mjs, repair the actual module, add candidate.test.mjs with meaningful tests, run tests, and write deliverable.json exactly {schema_version:1,summary:string,tests_run:string[],limitations:string[]} and nonempty notes.md with actual validation and limits. A final chat answer alone is not completion. Remembered experience is scoped reference data; this contract controls where source policies differ. No further human answers will arrive. Stop within 16 model responses,60 tool calls,300 seconds. Do not claim checks you did not run.

result.content: export function plan({zone,range_start,range_end,rules,exclusions,busy}){const out=[];for(let day=Date.parse(range_start.slice(0,10)+'T00:00Z');day<Date.parse(range_end);day+=86400000){const local_date=new Date(day).toISOString().slice(0,10);for(const r of rules){if(new Date(day).getUTCDay()!==r.weekday||local_date<r.from||local_date>r.through)continue;const start=Date.parse(local_date+'T'+r.start+'Z'),end=start+r.minutes*60000;if(start<Date.parse(range_start)||end>Date.parse(range_end))continue;if(busy.some(b=>start<Date.parse(b.end)&&Date.parse(b.start)<end))continue;out.push({rule_id:r.id,local_date,start:new Date(start).toISOString(),end:new Date(end).toISOString()});}}return out.sort((a,b)=>Date.parse(a.start)-Date.parse(b.start)||a.rule_id.localeCompare(b.rule_id));}

# Repair and validation

The module enumerates absolute minutes and obtains local labels through Intl.DateTimeFormat with the requested zone and a 00–23 hour cycle. Missing local times therefore never appear, while repeated times remain distinct absolute instants. Occurrences are grouped independently by rule and local date, then fold selection happens before containment or busy filtering. A day of padding ensures that the other side of a fold is considered even when outside the query.

Durations are elapsed milliseconds. Busy conflicts use strict half-open overlap inequalities. Exclusions are keyed by rule ID and local date. Results retain distinct rules and resolved instants and sort by UTC start followed by ASCII ID comparison. Input arrays and objects are not modified.

## Actual validation

Ran functions.tests after writing solution.mjs and candidate.test.mjs. Both public tests and nine candidate tests passed: 11 total, 0 failures. Tests cover New York fold modes and gap, fold selection before range/busy filtering, Berlin gap and fold, Lord Howe half-hour changes, Kathmandu's fractional offset and local date, explicit offset query and busy endpoints, elapsed duration across a fold, midnight crossing, inclusive rule dates, range equality, adjacent busy intervals versus true overlap, per-rule exclusions, ASCII ordering, frozen inputs, and a fourteen-day query crossing a year boundary.

## Limits

Inputs are assumed well formed as contracted; there is no added validation for invalid IDs, dates, zones, or ranges. Minute enumeration and one-day padding target the specified five zones in 2024–2026 and at most fourteen elapsed days. Those zones have minute-aligned offsets and folds no larger than one hour in this period. This is not a general resolver for historical sub-minute offsets or multi-day date-line changes. Timezone rules come from the installed Node Intl database. No live calendar, network, or third-party package was accessed. No additional test suites or exhaustive transition matrix were run.
